title: Integrating Unemployed but Employable Persons with Disabilities into Singapore Core
what_it_is: Integrating Unemployed but Employable Persons with Disabilities into Singapore Core

sections.label: Special needs employment programmes
sections.summary: Over 1,600 persons with special needs were placed in jobs in three years through programmes like ODP and Career Trial.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In the past three years, more than 1,600 persons with special needs have been placed, that is, found jobs, found placements, through these programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The ODP, which is administered by SG Enable, provides dedicated support for employers to hire, train and include persons with special needs in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Some employers may be unsure whether a particular person with special needs would be suited for the job, while persons with special needs may also be unsure whether the job and work environment are suitable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have the Career Trial programme which offers an opportunity for jobseekers to train and work for employers for a short stint of three months, during which time the jobseeker receives a training allowance from Workforce Singapore (WSG).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Since April 2018, all persons with special needs who are hired after the trial will receive retention incentives and their employers will also receive salary support.

sections.label: Disabled employment percentage figure
sections.summary: MSF reported 8,600 people with disabilities in employment, about 4.88% of the total.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As to what concerns me, and I think I have got to share with Members of the House that last week, it was reported that in terms of the number of people with disabilities who are in employment which was given by MSF as 8,600 to a Parliamentary Question I filed; against the total number of people of disabilities, we are looking at a percentage of about 4.88%.

sections.label: More comprehensive special needs data
sections.summary: The Government has begun collecting more comprehensive data and will release more accurate employment estimates later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: However, in recent years, the Government has also started to collect more comprehensive data on persons with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, in the meantime, just bear with us because we will be releasing more accurate estimates of the employment and unemployment rates for persons with special needs later this year, once we have a better picture of the situation.

sections.label: Open Door and Job Redesign grants
sections.summary: The Open Door Programme gives training grants up to 90%, and the Job Redesign Grant supports up to 90%, capped at $20,000 per worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If you look at the Open Door Programme, for example, we give training grants of up to 90% to employers to employ persons with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And if you look at the Job Redesign Grant, for example, we also support up to 90%, capped at $20,000 per special needs worker for employers to redesign jobs to employ them, to modify their work environment and processes to be more inclusive for persons with special needs.
